name: Grand piano (Steinway B)
note: An instrument recipe for the sampler (doc 24, Instruments, Sample preparation and Sampler rules). It describes exactly the files the prep step produced; nothing here is a tuning choice. type, id, name, version: what this is. source: where the recordings come from (library, folder url, license) and what the library's own note files say (notes). channels: channel count of every file. formats: each file exists once per format under root, as <file>.ogg (Ogg Opus, 48 kHz, 96 kbps stereo or 64 kbps mono, variable bitrate) and <file>.m4a (AAC-LC at the source rate, 128 kbps stereo or 96 kbps mono); the browser picks the first it can play. root: folder of the files, relative to the repo. layers: the number of velocity layers in the sustain set, layer 1 the quietest. sets: one entry per articulation: sus (sustain, pedal down or natural ring), nosus (dampers working), rel (release or key-off noise, played on note-off), pedal (sounds of the pedal mechanism). Each set has source (the library subfolder) and zones; a zone is one recorded key: note (scientific pitch, C4 = middle C, sharps written s in file names), midi (C4 = 60). measuredCents: the zone's measured pitch offset from 12-tone equal temperament at A4 = 440 Hz, in cents, as recorded; piano strings are inharmonic (partial n sits at n f0 sqrt(1 + B n^2)), so it is fitted from partials 1 to 6 (2 to 8 in the bass, where the fundamental is weak) over a window of the early sustain, each partial taken as the level-weighted centre of its unison-string cluster, and it is the pitch of the fitted first partial. Real pianos are stretch-tuned on purpose (bass flat, treble sharp); nothing has been corrected. tuneLayer: the layer the zone's number comes from (the middle one). tuneResidualCents: how far the found partials sit from the fit (root mean square, cents). tunePartials: which partials were found and used. layerSpreadCents: the largest difference between this zone's layers. inharmonicityB: the fitted B. unisonSplitCents: the widest spread seen inside one partial's cluster (a sign of unison strings tuned apart, which is heard as beating or chorus). tuneConfidence: 0 to 1, falls with fewer partials, a larger residual and a larger layer spread; below about 0.5 trust the ear over the number. layers: the files of the zone, quietest first; file is the path under root without extension; layer is its velocity layer and rr its round-robin take when the set has takes. peakDb: the file's sample peak in dBFS. attackRmsDb: the RMS level of its first 300 ms after the onset, in dBFS. Whether these levels mean anything depends on the source (see levels below). brightness: the share of energy above 1.5 times the note's fundamental (or 1 kHz, whichever is higher) in those first 300 ms, which should rise from layer to layer; in a very quiet file the noise floor can inflate it. lenS: length after the prep, in seconds. trimStartMs: how much was cut from the start (the onset, the first point above -50 dB of the file's peak, is kept with 3 ms before it). measuredCents on a layer is that file's own measurement. src: the original file name. Every file was cut where its 50 ms RMS fell to 60 dB below its peak, or at a maximum length (8 s at A0 falling evenly per semitone to 4 s at C8 for sustains, 2 s for releases), whichever came first, then given an equal-power fade over its last 250 ms (100 ms for releases and pedal sounds) so it ends in true silence. No gain was changed. levels: whether the source normalised each file (normalized true: the levels say nothing about how hard the key was played, so the sampler rebuilds the dynamic range from velocity with its own curve and must not re-gain the layers) or kept the recorded levels (normalized false: the layers already step up in level as they were played, and the sampler should play them at their own level). range: the lowest and highest sustain zone. problems: anything odd found while preparing, in plain words. The .m4a files decode about 23 ms longer than the .ogg files because AAC pads its last frame with silence; the start is in the same place in both. Steinway B: rel has a release sample per layer for most zones; a zone without one should fall back to the nearest zone's release. GAME SET (Matt, October 19, 2026): the middle five octaves only (zones A#1 to D7), tails cut to 4 s with a 250 ms fade, notes below C3 folded to mono, encoded Opus at 90 kbps stereo and 60 kbps mono (10.2 MB with the pedal, no-pedal and key-off sets) with AAC at 128 and 80 kbps; every file's peak, attack loudness, length and channels re-measured after shaping (the mono notes came out about 1.3 dB quieter, which the leveling corrects). gameSet records these choices.

source.notes: Folder 'Grand Piano, Steinway B', close mic, recorded by JH (files JHPiano_*). Subfolders: Sus (sustain pedal held down while recording), NoSus (dampers working normally), Rel (the release noise of the NoSus notes, files named NoSusRel). Velocity layers in the source are vl2, vl3 and vl4 (there is no vl1); here they are renumbered v1, v2, v3, quietest first. One round robin (rr1) only, so file names carry no rr. NORMALIZED.txt says: the sustain and no-sustain articulations were normalised; use a velocity curve to rebuild dynamic range and do not adjust the gain of layers or they will not line up. We followed it: no gain change, levels measured and recorded. The release set is not normalised (its peaks sit 30 to 64 dB below full scale) and keeps its recorded level. Note names in the files are standard scientific pitch (A#0 is the second-lowest A-sharp of the keyboard, C4 middle C), confirmed by pitch measurement.

levels.note: Sus and NoSus were normalised per file by the library (peaks -0.2 to -12 dBFS); rebuild dynamics with a velocity curve and never re-gain layers. Rel keeps its recorded level (peaks -29 to -64 dBFS).

range.playable: A1 to D#7 (each zone stretches a semitone either way)

problems: Steinway rel has no release samples from E6 up. That is expected: the top strings of a grand have no dampers, so there is nothing to release.
nosus: brightness does not rise with layer in 3 of 42 zones: Fs6 (v1 0.001, v2 0.000, v3 0.003); E7 (v1 0.000, v2 0.000, v3 0.000); Fs7 (v1 0.000, v2 0.000, v3 0.000)

sus: layers of the same key disagree in pitch by more than 5 cents in 1 zones (usually a high, fast-dying note or a unison that beats; the zone number uses the middle layer): Gs7 (v1 +6.0, v2 +5.6, v3 +20.6)

nosus: layers of the same key disagree in pitch by more than 5 cents in 5 zones (usually a high, fast-dying note or a unison that beats; the zone number uses the middle layer): Fs6 (v1 +6.7, v2 -0.9, v3 -0.7); As6 (v1 +6.2, v2 -2.4, v3 +1.7); C7 (v1 +16.4, v2 +9.2, v3 +8.9); D7 (v1 +17.8, v2 +9.5, v3 +10.4); Fs7 (v1 +18.3, v2 +10.2, v3 +9.1)
rel: no release sample for 9 sus zones: E6, Fs6, Gs6, As6, C7, D7, E7, Fs7, Gs7

mobile.note: MOBILE SET: the lighter piano phones play (doc 24, Performance budget); the sampler uses it in place of sets, layers and root when its tier is 'mobile', and the desktop keeps the game set above. It is made from the same processed recordings as the game set: zones every major third (A#1, D2, F#2 ... D7, the game set's range), two velocity layers, tails cut to tailS seconds with the game set's 250 ms quarter-cosine fade, mono throughout, encoded Opus at opusKbps and AAC at aacKbps. Mono is the left microphone alone (monoFrom): the library's two close microphones are spaced, and averaging them cancels part of some notes (A#3, F#5, D6 and A#6 lost 4 to 11 dB of their attack, a hollow sound), while the left microphone alone has no cancellation and keeps the pair's colour best. layerFrom says which recording of the game set each mobile layer is (layer 1 the softer): pedal down uses the softest and loudest (v1, v3); without pedal the softest recording (v1) is almost a pure tone, about twenty times duller than the pedal-down v1, so the no-pedal set uses v2 and v3, which match the pedal-down pair in brightness and keep a chord change (where the pedal lifts) from changing colour. File names are those of the game set's recording each one was made from (sus/D4-v3 is the game set's sus/D4-v3, shortened and mono), so layer, not the name, is the mobile layer. The loud layer of each pedal and no-pedal zone is moved by alignMs milliseconds (at most 1 ms, positive later) so its attack lines up in phase with the soft one: in a velocity blend the two recordings sound together, and out of phase they partly cancelled (up to 4.8 dB lost at A#6); lined up, every zone's blend now rises by the same 1.5 to 1.6 dB. Every file's peak, attack loudness, length, brightness and pitch were measured again from the encoded file (decoded at 48 kHz), the same way as the game set; a zone's measuredCents is the mean of its two layers, layerSpreadCents their difference, and tuneConfidence follows the first prep's rule. There are no key-off sounds: unpacked for a piece they would add 5 to 6 MB (all the layers of each zone a piece touches), and the pedal and no-pedal notes alone already come to about 9 to 14 MB a piece (median 12), at the phone budget. pedalNoise: the Knight upright's pedal mechanism for phones, one press and one lift (down-1, up-1; the desktop has four of each), cut to tailS with the same fade, left microphone, then brought to the stereo files' attack loudness (the sampler plays the pedal at a fixed level). downloadMB: what a phone downloads; decodedMB: the memory once every file is unpacked at 48 kHz (the sampler unpacks only what a piece uses).

range.playable: A1 to D#7 (each zone stretches two semitones either way)
